note: DRAFT v1 module checks and final knowledge check for the CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner course. Original CARSI questions written for Australian and New Zealand conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced. Answer positions balanced (each option position holds a quarter of correct answers). SME review and sign-off required before seeding.

quizzes.title: CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner — Module 1 check

questions.questionText: Under the model WHS laws, who holds the primary duty of care for workers on a fire job?
options: The property owner who rang to book the job
The insurer that has accepted and will pay the claim
The person conducting the business or undertaking (PCBU)
The most senior technician who is on site that day
questions.explanation: The model WHS laws put the primary duty of care on the PCBU. New Zealand’s HSWA places the same primary duty on the PCBU.

questions.questionText: Which law governs workplace health and safety on a fire job in Victoria?
options: The Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004
The model WHS Act, as in every other state
The Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (NZ)
No workplace safety act applies to restoration
questions.explanation: The model WHS laws apply everywhere in Australia except Victoria, where the OHS Act 2004 applies and WorkSafe Victoria regulates. HSWA 2015 is New Zealand law.

questions.questionText: Which order follows the fire restoration arc taught in this course?
options: Clean, deodorise, assess, then make the site safe last
Assess, deodorise, clean, remove the source, then verify
Make safe, deodorise, clean, then remove the source
Make safe, assess, mitigate, remove source, clean, odour, verify
questions.explanation: Each step changes what the next one finds: deodorising before source removal only masks odour, and cleaning before the hazard check can spread asbestos or lead.

questions.questionText: A worker is seriously injured on a fire job in Hamilton, New Zealand. What must the PCBU do?
options: Raise it at the weekly toolbox meeting, then report it
Notify WorkSafe as soon as possible by the fastest means
Report it only if emergency services did not attend
Tell the insurer, who passes the report on to WorkSafe
questions.explanation: Under HSWA a PCBU must notify WorkSafe as soon as possible, by the fastest means available, even if emergency services attend, and keep records for at least five years.

questions.questionText: An air scrubber draws 2.5 A and a HEPA vacuum 4.3 A on one 10 A circuit. How much headroom is left?
questions.explanation: 2.5 + 4.3 = 6.8 A, so a 10 A circuit has 3.2 A left. A 3.9 A dehumidifier would overload it, so it goes on a second circuit once an electrician confirms it is safe.

questions.questionText: A kitchen is 3.6 m by 3.0 m with a 2.4 m ceiling. What are its floor area and air volume?
options: 6.6 m² and about 15.8 m³
10.8 m² and about 108 m³
25.9 m² and about 10.8 m³
10.8 m² and about 25.9 m³
questions.explanation: 3.6 × 3.0 = 10.8 m² of floor; 10.8 × 2.4 ≈ 25.9 m³ of air. Record each room separately.

quizzes.title: CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner — Module 2 check

questions.questionText: What does PM2.5 describe?
options: Particles under 2.5 microns that can reach deep into the lungs
Smoke that has cooled to below 2.5 °C after the fire
A residue layer about 2.5 mm thick on painted surfaces
A respirator filter rated for 2.5 hours of continuous use
questions.explanation: Australian health advice describes PM2.5 as particles under 2.5 microns that, when breathed in, go deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream.

questions.questionText: A couch smouldered for hours before the alarm. What residue would you expect to test for first?
options: A dry, powdery residue that smears very little
No residue, because smouldering fires burn clean
A wet, smeary residue with a strong smell
Only a fuel-oil residue from the heater
questions.explanation: Slow, low-oxygen smouldering fires tend to leave wetter, smeary residue with a strong smell. Treat it as a hypothesis and confirm with test patches.

questions.questionText: Why can an upstairs bedroom smell strongly of smoke while showing little soot?
options: Smoke odour only travels downward through a building
The smell comes from fresh paint, not from the fire itself
Soot always collects inside the HVAC filter, not on rooms
Porous materials absorbed odour compounds carried in the smoke
questions.explanation: Carpet, upholstery, plasterboard and timber absorb odour-causing compounds, so odour and visible soot do not always match. Survey every room.

questions.questionText: Which pathway carries smoke up a stairwell to rooms well above a ground-floor fire?
options: Deposition on cool surfaces
Absorption into carpet
The stack effect
Test-patch transfer
questions.explanation: Warm, smoke-laden air rises through stairwells, risers and cavities, carrying smoke to upper floors and the roof space.

questions.questionText: Why does the assessment record a boundary between affected and unaffected areas?
options: It is only needed when asbestos has been found on the job
It sets the scope, quote and cleaning plan; assessors check it
It replaces the need to take photographs of every room
It tells the owner which rooms they can clean themselves
questions.explanation: The boundary, recorded with what you saw, smelt and measured, sets the scope and is the first thing an insurer’s assessor will check.

questions.questionText: Five doors each have a 10 mm gap under an 820 mm leaf. What is the total open gap?
options: About 0.041 m²
About 4.1 m²
About 0.0082 m²
About 0.41 m²
questions.explanation: 10 × 820 = 8,200 mm² = 0.0082 m² per door; five doors ≈ 0.041 m², about the size of a 200 mm square hole.

quizzes.title: CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner — Module 3 check

questions.questionText: Which build-date rule should trigger "suspect asbestos" on a fire job?
options: Australia: only buildings built before 1990; NZ: before 2000
Both countries: only buildings built before 1970
AU: built or renovated before the 2003 ban; NZ: before 2000
Australia: before 2000; NZ: only buildings built before 1990
questions.explanation: In Australia, assume asbestos may be present in any building built or renovated before the national ban took effect on 31 December 2003; pre-1990 buildings are the most likely to contain it. In New Zealand, any building built or renovated before 2000 could contain asbestos (WorkSafe NZ).

questions.questionText: Fire has cracked 8.1 m² of fibre-cement eaves lining in a 1972 house. Who removes it?
options: A Class A licensed asbestos removalist
Anyone, because it is under 10 m²
A Class B removalist, because it was non-friable
The restoration crew, if they wear P2 masks
questions.explanation: Fire-damaged asbestos is treated as friable (NSW EPA; WorkSafe NZ reclassifies it), so it is Class A work whatever its area. The 10 m² exemption no longer applies.

questions.questionText: What is the restorer’s first action on finding suspect fire-damaged asbestos debris?
options: Sweep it into bags quickly before it spreads any further
Hose it down with high-pressure water to settle the dust
Vacuum it with the household vacuum cleaner already on site
Stop, leave it undisturbed, keep people out and hand it over
questions.explanation: Stop, isolate and hand the area to a licensed assessor and Class A removalist. Cleaning in that area waits for clearance.

questions.questionText: How do the Australian and New Zealand silica exposure standards compare?
options: Both are 0.05 mg/m³
Australia 0.05 mg/m³; New Zealand 0.025 mg/m³
Australia 0.025 mg/m³; New Zealand 0.05 mg/m³
Both are 0.1 mg/m³
questions.explanation: Australia’s RCS standard is 0.05 mg/m³ (8-hour TWA) and stays there at the 1 December 2026 WEL switch. WorkSafe NZ lowered its standard to 0.025 mg/m³ in November 2023.

questions.questionText: A 1978 house in Tauranga has fire-blistered paint. What should you presume?
options: That it is lead-free because it was built after 1970
That it may contain lead-based paint
That only exterior paint can contain lead
That fire has burnt off any lead
questions.explanation: WorkSafe NZ and Health New Zealand say to presume lead-based paint in buildings from the 1980s or earlier. Lead paint cannot be identified by its appearance.

questions.questionText: How should ash from a burnt CCA-treated pergola be handled?
options: Sweep it up dry and put it in the garden or organics bin
Hose it off the slab with high-pressure water
Dig it into the garden beds, where ash helps the soil
Moisten, shovel, double-bag and take it to landfill
questions.explanation: Treat CCA ash as containing copper, chromium and arsenic (up to 10 % by weight). Keep it wet, shovel it, bag it, and never bury it or put it in a garden or organics bin.

quizzes.title: CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner — Module 4 check

questions.questionText: After a pot burnt dry on the stove, walls show a faint yellow film and a very strong smell. Which residue fits best?
options: Protein residue
Dry smoke residue
Fuel-oil residue
Wet smoke residue from foam
questions.explanation: Cooking fires leave a thin, near-invisible yellowish protein film with odour out of proportion to what you can see.

questions.questionText: Why test a cleaning method on a small patch before cleaning a whole surface?
options: Because insurers pay a set fee for every test patch done
To check whether the owner is happy with the colour first
To pick a method that will not damage the surface, and record it
Because test patches are only needed on glass and mirrors
questions.explanation: Starting with the least aggressive method on a hidden patch protects paint, finishes and fabrics, and the dated record protects you later.

questions.questionText: Dry, powdery soot covers a ceiling. What do you use first?
options: A wet cloth with detergent to lift the soot straight away
A pressure washer on low to rinse the ceiling clean
An ozone generator overnight before any cleaning starts
Dry methods: HEPA vacuuming and dry chemical sponges
questions.explanation: Liquid smears dry soot into the surface. Dry methods come first on dry residue, then wet methods only if the test patch shows they are needed.

questions.questionText: In which order should a room be cleaned?
options: Floor, then walls, then fixtures, then the ceiling last
Walls, then floor, then the ceiling, then the fixtures
Ceiling, then walls, then fixtures, then floor
Any order at all, as long as the crew works quickly
questions.explanation: Work top-down so falling residue lands on surfaces not yet cleaned, and work from the least to the most affected rooms.

questions.questionText: What must happen before charred materials are removed as source material?
options: The odour treatment for the whole of the house
The hazardous-materials check for that area
The final verification and the handover to the owner
Repainting the walls and ceilings in that room
questions.explanation: Source removal disturbs materials, so it comes after the asbestos, lead and ash checks (Module 3) have cleared that area.

questions.questionText: A 4.0 m by 3.4 m room has a 2.4 m ceiling, a 2.1 m² window and a 1.7 m² door. What is the wall area to clean?
options: About 31.7 m²
About 35.5 m²
About 13.6 m²
About 45.3 m²
questions.explanation: Perimeter 2 × (4.0 + 3.4) = 14.8 m; × 2.4 = 35.5 m²; less 3.8 m² of openings = 31.7 m². With the 13.6 m² ceiling the total is 45.3 m².

quizzes.title: CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner — Module 5 check

questions.questionText: Why does residue from burnt PVC threaten metal fittings and electronics?
options: PVC residue is magnetic, so it attracts metal dust onto fittings
PVC smoke only affects painted surfaces, not bare metal
Burning PVC forms hydrogen chloride, an acid that corrodes metal
It does not: only water from firefighting corrodes metal
questions.explanation: Hydrogen chloride from burning PVC deposits on materials, and studies show smoke causing pitting corrosion of stainless steel and aluminium alloy that worsens with time.

questions.questionText: What did corrosion research show about humidity and smoke?
options: Corrosion depends on factors including humidity and time
Humidity has no measurable effect on smoke corrosion
Only very dry air lets smoke residue corrode metal
Corrosion stops completely after the first hour or so
questions.explanation: Studies used high humidity and found corrosion depends on the metal, temperature, humidity, exposure time and surface. Lowering humidity is part of mitigation.

questions.questionText: The owner wants to switch on smoke-filmed point-of-sale terminals to see if they work. What do you advise?
options: Switch them on, then clean them only if they fail to start
Spray them with water to rinse the residue, then switch on
Run them for an hour so the heat dries out the residue
Do not power them; isolate, document and refer to a specialist
questions.explanation: Powering a contaminated board can turn a cleanable item into a loss. Isolate it and refer it to an electronics restoration specialist.

questions.questionText: Which three groups are used to triage fire-affected contents?
options: Clean, dirty and very dirty, sorted by how they look
Restore on site, restore off site, total loss
Owner’s, tenant’s and insurer’s, by who paid for them
Keep, sell and donate, as the owner prefers
questions.explanation: Every item is photographed and inventoried, then placed in one of the three groups before it is cleaned or moved.

questions.questionText: A ducted system ran for an hour after the fire. What is the rule for it?
options: Run it on high for a day to clear the smoke from the house
Keep it off until professionally cleaned and filters replaced
Replace the filter and switch it straight back on again
Ignore it, because ductwork is outside the restoration scope
questions.explanation: Running a contaminated system re-contaminates rooms you have already cleaned. Assess outlets, filters, coil and ductwork and record any referral.

questions.questionText: A 72.9 m³ kitchen holds about 86 kg of air. Air drops from 17.0 to 10.5 g/kg. About how much water leaves the air?
options: About 5.6 kg
About 56 kg
About 0.056 kg
About 0.56 kg
questions.explanation: 17.0 − 10.5 = 6.5 g/kg; 6.5 × 86 ≈ 559 g ≈ 0.56 kg. The air dries fast, but wet materials keep feeding it.

quizzes.title: CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner — Module 6 check

questions.questionText: Which order controls smoke odour?
options: Remove the source, clean, seal, treat remaining odour, verify
Treat with a device, then clean, then remove the source
Seal everything first, then clean the surfaces, then verify
Verify first, then remove the source, then clean and seal
questions.explanation: Odour is residue. Device treatments work only after source removal and cleaning; sealing locks in what cannot be cleaned.

questions.questionText: What are the ozone workplace limits in Australia and New Zealand?
options: Australia 1 ppm peak; New Zealand 0.1 ppm ceiling
Australia 0.1 ppm peak; New Zealand has no ozone limit
Both 0.1 ppm (0.2 mg/m³): AU peak limit, NZ ceiling
Both 0.5 ppm as an eight-hour time-weighted average
questions.explanation: Australia: peak limitation of 0.1 ppm (0.2 mg/m³). New Zealand: WES ceiling of 0.1 ppm (0.2 mg/m³), not to be exceeded at any time.

questions.questionText: A tenant returns tomorrow morning. Can an overnight ozone treatment go ahead?
options: Yes, as long as the windows are opened at 6 am to air it out
Yes, because 0.1 ppm is a safe level for the occupants too
Yes, if the tenant sleeps in another room with the door shut
No: ozone needs an empty space; re-entry is decided on readings
questions.explanation: The 0.1 ppm figure is a worker limit, not occupant clearance. Re-entry is a site-specific decision based on the manufacturer’s instructions and calibrated readings.

questions.questionText: A supplier says a hydroxyl unit is safe with the family at home. What does this course advise?
options: Accept it, because the unit is not an ozone generator
Run it at double the setting so the odour clears faster
Ask for an independent test report; keep people out until known
Use it in the bedrooms only, where the family sleeps
questions.explanation: A 2021 study measured organic acids and new particles forming while a hydroxyl generator ran. The CARSI Ozone course recommends keeping people out until you know what yours produces.

questions.questionText: Under New Zealand’s Consumer Guarantees Act, how must a restoration service be carried out?
options: Only in the way the insurer directs, whatever the result
With reasonable care and skill, and fit for purpose
At the lowest possible price the restorer can offer
Within 24 hours of the fire, whatever the job size
questions.explanation: The CGA guarantees services are carried out with reasonable care and skill and are fit for purpose. In Australia the ACL requires an acceptable level of care and skill.

questions.questionText: A clean-and-seal stage is A$3,850 excluding GST. What is the price including Australian GST?
questions.explanation: Australian GST is 10 %: 3,850 × 0.10 = 385, so 3,850 + 385 = A$4,235. Show the area, rate and GST separately.

quizzes.title: CARSI Fire & Smoke Restoration Practitioner — Final knowledge check

questions.questionText: Why must the hazardous-materials check come before any cleaning on a fire job?
options: Cleaning chemicals do not work on hazardous materials
The insurer requires the check for billing purposes only
Cleaning can disturb and spread asbestos, lead dust or toxic ash
It does not: cleaning can start straight away on arrival
questions.explanation: The arc puts make-safe and the hazard check first because wiping, brushing and source removal disturb materials and put contaminants into the air.

questions.questionText: Which statement about PM2.5 is correct?
options: They are small enough to reach deep into the lungs and blood
They are large enough to see as flakes of ash on surfaces
They only exist outdoors during bushfires, never indoors
They become harmless as soon as the fire has been put out
questions.explanation: PM2.5 particles are under 2.5 microns. They can linger and reach dangerous levels inside buildings after the fire.

questions.questionText: A 1995 house in Nelson, New Zealand, has fire-cracked cladding. Should you suspect asbestos?
options: No: asbestos stopped being used everywhere in 1990
No: cladding products never contained any asbestos
Only if the house is in Australia, not New Zealand
Yes: in New Zealand, buildings before 2000 may contain it
questions.explanation: WorkSafe NZ says any building built or renovated before 2000 could contain asbestos. In Australia the rule is any building built or renovated before the 31 December 2003 ban, with pre-1990 buildings the most likely.

questions.questionText: Who removes fire-damaged asbestos-containing material in either country?
options: A Class B licensed asbestos removalist
A Class A licensed asbestos removalist
The restoration crew wearing P2 respirators
The property owner, with council approval
questions.explanation: NSW EPA treats fire-impacted ACM as friable (Class A); WorkSafe NZ says to reclassify it as friable and use a Class A removalist.

questions.questionText: A cutting method keeps a crew at 0.04 mg/m³ of respirable crystalline silica. Which statement is correct?
options: Under both the Australian and New Zealand standards
Under the AU standard but above the NZ standard
Above both the Australian and New Zealand standards
Above the AU standard but under the NZ standard
questions.explanation: Australia: 0.05 mg/m³. New Zealand: 0.025 mg/m³. 0.04 sits between them.

questions.questionText: How much copper, chromium and arsenic can CCA ash and char contain by weight?
options: Up to 0.1 %
Up to 50 %
None once burnt
Up to 10 %
questions.explanation: EPA Victoria and Queensland Health say the ash and char can contain up to 10 % by weight copper, chromium and arsenic.

questions.questionText: Which residue is a thin yellowish film from a cooking fire, with a very strong smell?
options: Protein residue
Dry smoke residue
Fuel-oil residue
Wet smoke residue
questions.explanation: Protein residue is near-invisible but discolours paint and varnish, and its odour is out of proportion to what you see.

questions.questionText: Which cleaning approach suits dry, powdery soot?
options: A wet wipe first, so the soot does not become airborne
A solvent degreaser first, to cut through the film
Dry methods first: HEPA vacuum and dry chemical sponge
High-pressure water first, then a dry sponge to finish
questions.explanation: Liquids smear dry soot into the surface; dry methods come first, then wet methods only if testing shows they are needed.

questions.questionText: What did a study of smoke from many materials find about corrosion?
options: Only the smoke from burning PVC was found to be corrosive
No smoke was corrosive when held at 75 % relative humidity
Corrosion only happened on metal heated above 100 °C
All smokes tested were corrosive, varying with metal and humidity
questions.explanation: Hirschler and Smith found all smokes tested were corrosive, with corrosion depending on metal, temperature, humidity, exposure time and surface.

questions.questionText: A ducted system is filmed with soot inside. When can it run again?
options: Straight away, as long as it runs on recirculation
After the carpet and soft furnishings have been cleaned
Once professionally cleaned with its filters replaced
Once the smell of smoke in the house has faded
questions.explanation: A contaminated system re-contaminates cleaned rooms, so it stays off and isolated until cleaned.

questions.questionText: What is the workplace ozone limit in both Australia and New Zealand?
options: 1.0 ppm as an eight-hour time-weighted average
0.1 ppm (0.2 mg/m³), not to be exceeded at any time
0.5 ppm averaged over any 15-minute period
There is no ozone limit in either country
questions.explanation: Australia has a peak limitation of 0.1 ppm and New Zealand a ceiling of 0.1 ppm. It is a worker limit, not clearance for occupants.

questions.questionText: ICNZ advice to New Zealand policyholders after a fire is to contact the insurer when?
options: As soon as they can and before having any work done
Only after all of the repairs have been finished
Only if the damage looks expensive to put right
Any time within 12 months of the fire
questions.explanation: ICNZ advises contacting the insurer before any work is done. For the restorer, get scope approval before work beyond emergency mitigation.
